wins.label: Record GBM revenues and strong diversification
wins.evidence: Global Banking & Markets produced record revenues of $12.7 billion in the first quarter and generated an ROE of over 22%

wins.label: Strong M&A leadership and pipeline
wins.evidence: We remain #1 in the league tables for M&A with a lead of $150 billion in announced volumes versus our closest peer. Our backlog closed 2025 at its highest level in 4 years

wins.label: Robust equity financing growth
wins.evidence: Record Equities financing revenues of $2.6 billion were 59% higher year-over-year with particular strength in Asia amid another record for average prime balances

wins.label: Consistent AWM inflows and client engagement
wins.evidence: We generated $62 billion in long-term fee-based inflows, including $22 billion in Wealth Management flows. 33rd consecutive quarter of long-term fee-based net inflows

wins.label: Strong private credit positioning with institutional demand
wins.evidence: 40% of first quarter 2026 subscriptions in our GS credit BDC were from institutions, many of whom are first-time investors. Over 80% institutional partners very broad and diverse

risks.label: Geopolitical uncertainty and energy price volatility
risks.evidence: Heightened uncertainty in parts of private credit and the conflict in the Middle East. If the resolution of the conflict drags, that probably will be a headwind in some of these areas particularly inflation trends

risks.label: Private credit industry scrutiny and retail redemptions
risks.evidence: There are obviously heightened redemptions in certain peer managed funds. These peer managed funds have been concentrated in retail outflows as opposed to institutional outflows

risks.label: Weaker FICC intermediation in rates and mortgages
risks.evidence: Within intermediation, revenues in rates and mortgages were significantly lower versus the first quarter of last year as results were impacted by a tougher market-making backdrop

risks.label: Sponsor activity and IPO slowdown
risks.evidence: While market conditions tempered execution for IPOs and sponsor activity broadly. IPO activity slowed a little bit, particularly in March

risks.label: Long credit cycle and potential for elevated losses
risks.evidence: This has been a long period of time without a normal credit cycle, meaning a meaningful slowdown in the economy, or a recession. When credit cycles go on longer, spreads get tighter, market participants get more aggressive to deploy capital
